title: Linux Terminal Fundamentals
description: A beginner-friendly Linux course focused on terminal navigation, files, folders, safe command habits, and workspace-based practice.
audience: cybersecurity students who need Linux basics
goals: Use pwd, ls, ls -a, and cd to inspect and navigate an existing Linux workspace
Create, copy, move, rename, and safely remove specific workspace files after instruction
Write and append short text with echo, >, and >>; verify it with cat, head, tail, and wc -l
Complete the Community Media Archive using inspect first, change second, verify last

teachingStyle.tone: friendly, practical, beginner-safe, terminal-first, and project-oriented

notes: Use shell_task terminal_workspace code_input items for Linux terminal practice.
Use workspaceExpectations for file-tree checks and terminalExpectations for output/command checks.
Use per-exercise terminal workspaces for independent quiz/check exercises.
Prepend a standalone reading-only course welcome without replacing the first technical sketch.
Use book-like technical prose and concept-specific help.
Keep the final capstone in one section and one topic with five cumulative Community Media Archive steps.
Remind learners to press Enter after each terminal command in every terminal-workspace exercise prompt.
Module 1 Terminal Map uses pre-seeded paths; do not introduce mkdir/touch until Module 2.
Module 2 must cover echo, >, >>, and safe single-file rm before the capstone.
Retain stable published IDs even when learner-facing titles are corrected.
